name: room
text: Room opened — goal: creators: Build PACKAGES + enrich tabs + draft elements; every one labeled 'Created by EXCAVA' + tes

name: Forge
text: We should focus on building packages first, as this will give us a solid foundation for the rest of our work. By doing so, we'll be able to create a consistent structure that will make it easier to enrich tabs and draft elements later on. This decision means we'll be delaying the enrichment of tabs and drafting of elements, but I believe it's a trade-off worth accepting because it will save us time and effort in the long run by reducing the need for rework and revisions. By prioritizing package building, we'll be putting quality first and setting ourselves up for success in achieving our goal.

name: Vet
text: Vet: Hold on—delaying tab enrichment isn’t just a delay, it’s a hidden bet that the package structure will *stay* solid enough to build on. What if the packages force us to redo tabs later because they’re too rigid? Instead, why not prototype one tab *while* building the first package? That way, we test both at once and spot mismatches early. Settle it by building a tiny tab mockup against the first package draft—if it breaks, we pivot; if it works, we scale.
